name: VITAMIN B1 (THIAMINE)
interpretation: Serum Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) measures thiamine concentration. Thiamine is a coenzyme for pyruvate dehydrogenase, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, and transketolase. Deficiency: beriberi (wet: cardiac, dry: neurological), Wernicke encephalopathy (confusion, ataxia, ophthalmoplegia). Thiamine: essential for glucose metabolism. Reference ranges: method-specific.
pre_analytical: Sample: Serum or whole blood. Standard venipuncture. Preparation: note alcohol use, malnutrition, neurological symptoms. Handle per standard. Deficiency: beriberi, Wernicke. Alcohol: risk. Reference ranges: method-specific.
ref_ranges: Normal: 70 to 180 nmol/L (method-specific). Deficiency: less than 70. Beriberi: wet/dry. Reference ranges: method-specific.
refs: Sources: EFSA Thiamine Guidelines; manufacturer IFU.

name: VITAMIN B12
interpretation: Serum Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) measures the concentration of cobalamin in serum. Vitamin B12 is essential for DNA synthesis, red blood cell formation, and neurological function. Deficiency causes megaloblastic anaemia (macrocytosis, hypersegmented neutrophils) and subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord. Serum B12 is the initial screening test, but low B12 alone does not confirm deficiency as levels may be normal in the presence of functional deficiency. Serum methylmalonic acid (MMA) and homocysteine are more specific markers: elevated MMA and/or homocysteine with low B12 confirms functional deficiency. Causes of low B12: pernicious anaemia (most common cause in developed countries), gastrectomy, ileal resection or Crohn disease, vegan diet, metformin use, proton pump inhibitor use, bacterial overgrowth, fish tapeworm infection, congenital transcobalamin deficiency. Causes of elevated B12: liver disease (release from damaged hepatocytes), myeloproliferative disorders (excess production), leukaemia, polycythaemia vera, folic acid supplementation (masks deficiency). Limitations: serum B12 does not distinguish between deficiency and functional deficiency. Biotin supplementation may interfere on some immunoassay platforms. Reference ranges: method-specific. Age: B12 levels decline with age. Gender: may vary.
pre_analytical: Sample: Serum. Standard venipuncture. No fasting required. Preparation: note neurological symptoms (paraesthesia, numbness, gait disturbance), macrocytosis, medications (metformin, PPI, oral contraceptives), diet (vegan, vegetarian), family history of pernicious anaemia. Handling: separate within 30 min. Low B12: deficiency. Confirm with: MMA and homocysteine. High B12: liver disease, MPD. Biotin: interference on some platforms. Reference ranges: method-specific.
ref_ranges: Low: less than 200 pg/mL (deficiency). Low normal: 200 to 300 pg/mL (grey zone, confirm with MMA). Normal: 300 to 900 pg/mL. Elevated: greater than 900 pg/mL (liver disease, MPD, leukaemia). MMA elevated: confirms functional deficiency. Reference ranges: method-specific. Age: declines with age.
refs: Sources: BSH Vitamin B12 Guidelines; manufacturer IFU.

name: VITAMIN B2 (RIBOFLAVIN)
interpretation: Serum Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin) measures riboflavin concentration. Riboflavin is a precursor of FAD and FMN coenzymes essential for energy metabolism, antioxidant defence (glutathione reductase), and drug metabolism. Deficiency: ariboflavinosis (angular stomatitis, glossitis, cheilosis, corneal vascularisation). Reference ranges: method-specific.
pre_analytical: Sample: Serum. Standard venipuncture. No fasting required. Preparation: note malnutrition, malabsorption, alcohol use. Handle per standard. Deficiency: ariboflavinosis. FAD: coenzyme. Reference ranges: method-specific.
ref_ranges: Normal: variable (method-specific). Deficiency: ariboflavinosis. FAD: coenzyme. Reference ranges: method-specific.
refs: Sources: EFSA Riboflavin Guidelines; manufacturer IFU.

name: VITAMIN B6 (PYRIDOXINE/PYRIDOXAL 5-PHOSPHATE)
interpretation: Serum Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine/Pyridoxal 5-Phosphate) measures pyridoxal 5-phosphate (PLP), the active coenzyme form. PLP: coenzyme for over 100 enzymatic reactions including transamination, decarboxylation, and amino acid metabolism. Deficiency: sideroblastic anaemia, peripheral neuropathy, convulsions, dermatitis. Excess: sensory neuropathy (from supplementation). Reference ranges: method-specific.
pre_analytical: Sample: Serum (fasting preferred). Standard venipuncture. Preparation: note anaemia, neuropathy, seizures, oral contraceptive use. Handle per standard. Deficiency: sideroblastic anaemia. Excess: sensory neuropathy. Reference ranges: method-specific.
ref_ranges: Normal: 20 to 100 nmol/L (method-specific). Deficiency: less than 20. Excess: sensory neuropathy. Reference ranges: method-specific.
refs: Sources: EFSA Vitamin B6 Guidelines; manufacturer IFU.

name: VITAMIN C
interpretation: Serum Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid) measures ascorbic acid concentration. Vitamin C is an essential antioxidant required for collagen synthesis, iron absorption, immune function, and neurotransmitter metabolism. Deficiency: scurvy (bleeding gums, petechiae, poor wound healing, corkscrew hairs). Excess: oxalate nephropathy, kidney stones. Reference ranges: method-specific.
pre_analytical: Sample: Serum (fasting preferred). CRITICAL: light-protected tube, process within 1 hour. Preparation: note bleeding, poor wound healing, smoking. Handle: light-protected, process rapidly. Deficiency: scurvy. Excess: oxalate nephropathy. Reference ranges: method-specific.
ref_ranges: Normal: 0.4 to 2.0 mg/dL (method-specific). Deficiency: less than 0.2. Scurvy: less than 0.2. Reference ranges: method-specific.
refs: Sources: EFSA Vitamin C Guidelines; manufacturer IFU.

name: VITAMIN D 1 25-DIHYDROXY
interpretation: Serum 1,25-Dihydroxyvitamin D (Calcitriol) is the biologically active form of vitamin D. Calcitriol is produced in the kidney from 25-hydroxyvitamin D and regulates calcium and phosphate homeostasis. Elevated: sarcoidosis, primary hyperparathyroidism, lymphoma. Low: chronic kidney disease, hypoparathyroidism, vitamin D-dependent rickets type I. Reference ranges: method-specific.
pre_analytical: Sample: Serum (fasting preferred). Standard venipuncture. Preparation: note bone disease, calcium disorders, renal disease. Handle per standard. Elevated: sarcoidosis, hyperparathyroidism. Low: CKD, hypoparathyroidism. Reference ranges: method-specific.
ref_ranges: Normal: 18 to 72 pg/mL (method-specific). Elevated: sarcoidosis, hyperparathyroidism. Low: CKD. Reference ranges: method-specific.
refs: Sources: KDIGO CKD-MBD Guidelines; manufacturer IFU.

name: VITAMIN D TOTAL
interpretation: Serum Vitamin D Total measures the total concentration of 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25-OH-D) in serum, which includes both vitamin D2 (ergocalciferol, from dietary/plant sources) and vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol, from sunlight/synthesis and animal sources). Vitamin D is the major regulator of calcium and phosphate homeostasis, and deficiency causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults. Serum 25-OH-D is the best indicator of vitamin D status as it reflects both dietary intake and cutaneous synthesis. Interpretation: less than 10 ng/mL severe deficiency, 10 to 20 ng/mL deficiency, 20 to 30 ng/mL insufficiency, 30 to 100 ng/mL sufficiency, greater than 100 ng/mL toxicity risk. Elevated vitamin D: excessive supplementation, granulomatous diseases (sarcoidosis, tuberculosis), primary hyperparathyroidism. Low vitamin D: inadequate sun exposure, malabsorption, liver disease, chronic kidney disease, phenytoin use, dark skin pigmentation. Limitations: 25-OH-D is bound to vitamin D binding protein (DBP) and albumin; conditions that alter binding proteins (pregnancy, OCP use, liver disease) may affect total 25-OH-D without changing free (bioavailable) vitamin D. Assay variability between immunoassay and LC-MS/MS methods is significant. Reference ranges: method-specific.
pre_analytical: Sample: Serum. Standard venipuncture. No fasting required. Preparation: note sun exposure, diet, supplements, medications (phenytoin, rifampicin), liver function, kidney function, pregnancy. Handling: separate within 30 min. Severe deficiency: less than 10 ng/mL. Deficiency: 10 to 20. Insufficiency: 20 to 30. Sufficiency: 30 to 100. Toxicity: greater than 100. DBP: affects total but not free. Assay: method-specific variability.
ref_ranges: Severe deficiency: less than 10 ng/mL. Deficiency: 10 to 20 ng/mL. Insufficiency: 20 to 30 ng/mL. Sufficiency: 30 to 100 ng/mL. Toxicity risk: greater than 100 ng/mL. Free vitamin D: not measured by standard assays. Assay: immunoassay versus LC-MS/MS variability. Reference ranges: method-specific.
refs: Sources: Endocrine Society Vitamin D Guidelines; IoM Vitamin D Guidelines; manufacturer IFU.

name: VITAMIN D TOTAL (D2+D3)
interpretation: Vitamin D Total (D2+D3) measures the combined concentration of 25-hydroxyvitamin D2 and 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 in serum. This is essentially the same test as Vitamin D Total but explicitly specifies that both forms are measured. Some immunoassays may have different cross-reactivity with D2 versus D3, potentially underestimating total vitamin D in patients taking ergocalciferol (D2) supplements. LC-MS/MS methods provide accurate separate quantification of D2 and D3 forms. Clinical utility is identical to Vitamin D Total: assessing vitamin D status, guiding supplementation, and monitoring treatment response. The distinction between D2 and D3 matters pharmacologically as D3 is approximately 87 percent more potent than D2 in raising and maintaining serum 25-OH-D concentrations. Limitations: same as Vitamin D Total. Some immunoassays may underdetect D2. Reference ranges: method-specific.
pre_analytical: Sample: Serum. Standard venipuncture. No fasting required. Preparation: note supplements (D2 vs D3), sun exposure, diet, medications, liver and kidney function. Handle per standard. D2+D3 combined: total 25-OH-D. D2: ergocalciferol (plant). D3: cholecalciferol (animal/sunlight). D3 more potent than D2. Assay: method-specific. Reference ranges: method-specific.
ref_ranges: Same as Vitamin D Total. D3 more potent than D2. D2 supplements: some immunoassays may underestimate. LC-MS/MS: accurate separate quantification. Reference ranges: method-specific.
refs: Sources: Endocrine Society Vitamin D Guidelines; manufacturer IFU.

name: VITAMIN E (TOCOPHEROL)
interpretation: Serum Vitamin E (Tocopherol) measures alpha-tocopherol concentration. Vitamin E is a lipid-soluble antioxidant that protects cell membranes from oxidative damage. Deficiency: haemolytic anaemia, spinocerebellar ataxia, peripheral neuropathy, retinopathy. Excess: increased bleeding risk (antagonises vitamin K). Reference ranges: method-specific.
pre_analytical: Sample: Serum (fasting preferred). Standard venipuncture. Preparation: note haemolysis, neurological symptoms, fat malabsorption. Handle per standard. Deficiency: haemolytic anaemia. Excess: bleeding risk. Reference ranges: method-specific.
ref_ranges: Normal: 5 to 20 mcg/mL (method-specific). Deficiency: less than 5. Haemolytic anaemia: risk. Reference ranges: method-specific.
refs: Sources: EFSA Vitamin E Guidelines; manufacturer IFU.

name: VITAMIN K1
interpretation: Serum Vitamin K1 (Phylloquinone) measures phylloquinone concentration. Vitamin K1 is essential for blood coagulation (factors II, VII, IX, X, protein C, protein S) and bone metabolism (osteocalcin carboxylation). Deficiency: coagulopathy, bleeding, increased PT/INR. Neonates: haemorrhagic disease of the newborn. Reference ranges: method-specific.
pre_analytical: Sample: Serum (fasting preferred). CRITICAL: light-protected tube. Standard venipuncture. Preparation: note bleeding, coagulopathy, warfarin therapy. Handle: light-protected. Deficiency: coagulopathy. Neonatal: HDN. Reference ranges: method-specific.
ref_ranges: Normal: 0.2 to 3.2 ng/mL (method-specific). Deficiency: coagulopathy. Warfarin: antagonist. Reference ranges: method-specific.
refs: Sources: ISTH Vitamin K Guidelines; manufacturer IFU.

name: VLDL CHOLESTEROL
interpretation: VLDL Cholesterol (VLDL-C) measures the cholesterol content of very low-density lipoproteins in serum. VLDL particles are produced by the liver and transport endogenous triglycerides to peripheral tissues. VLDL-C is usually calculated as triglycerides divided by 5 (Friedewald equation) when triglycerides are less than 400 mg/dL and fasting. Direct measurement methods are also available. Elevated VLDL-C is associated with atherogenic dyslipidaemia (high triglycerides, low HDL, small dense LDL) and increased cardiovascular risk. Elevated VLDL-C occurs in metabolic syndrome, diabetes mellitus, obesity, hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, and familial hypertriglyceridaemia. Limitations: VLDL-C is typically calculated not directly measured. The Friedewald calculation (VLDL-C equals triglycerides divided by 5) is unreliable when triglycerides exceed 400 mg/dL, in non-fasting samples, or in the presence of type III hyperlipidaemia. Reference ranges: method-specific. Age: increases with age.
pre_analytical: Sample: Serum. CRITICAL: fasting sample (8-12h). Preparation: note diabetes control, lipid medications, alcohol use, family history of lipid disorders. Handle per standard. Fasting: essential for calculation. Friedewald: VLDL-C equals TG divided by 5. Unreliable: TG greater than 400 mg/dL. Atherogenic: elevated VLDL-C. Reference ranges: method-specific.
ref_ranges: Normal: less than 30 mg/dL. Elevated: greater than 30 mg/dL (atherogenic). Friedewald: VLDL-C equals TG divided by 5. Unreliable: TG greater than 400. Metabolic syndrome: elevated. Reference ranges: method-specific.
refs: Sources: ACC/AHA Cholesterol Guidelines; manufacturer IFU.

name: VOLTAGE GATED POTASSIUM CHANNEL (VGKC)
interpretation: Serum Voltage-Gated Potassium Channel (VGKC) Antibodies detect autoantibodies against VGKC complex (LGI1, CASPR2 subunits). VGKC antibodies: associated with autoimmune encephalitis, limbic encephalitis, neuromyotonia (Isaac syndrome), Morvan syndrome. LGI1: faciobrachial dystonic seizures, hyponatraemia. CASPR2: neuromyotonia, neuropathic pain. Reference ranges: method-specific.
pre_analytical: Sample: Serum. Standard venipuncture. No fasting required. Preparation: note seizures, cognitive decline, neuropathic pain, hyponatraemia. Handle per standard. LGI1: seizures, hyponatraemia. CASPR2: neuromyotonia. Reference ranges: method-specific.
ref_ranges: Normal: negative. Positive: autoimmune encephalitis. LGI1/CASPR2: subunit-specific. Reference ranges: method-specific.
refs: Sources: AAN Autoimmune Encephalitis Guidelines; manufacturer IFU.

name: VORICONAZOLE
interpretation: Serum Voriconazole measures the concentration of voriconazole, a triazole antifungal used to treat invasive aspergillosis, candidemia, and other serious fungal infections. Therapeutic range: 1 to 5.5 mcg/mL. Toxic: greater than 5.5 mcg/mL (visual disturbances, hepatotoxicity, periostitis). Nonlinear pharmacokinetics: dose adjustments require TDM. Reference ranges: method-specific.
pre_analytical: Sample: Serum (trough level). CRITICAL: trough level. Preparation: note fungal infection, liver function, other medications. Handle per standard. Therapeutic: 1-5.5 mcg/mL. Toxic: greater than 5.5. Nonlinear: TDM essential. Reference ranges: method-specific.
ref_ranges: Therapeutic: 1 to 5.5 mcg/mL (trough). Toxic: greater than 5.5. Visual: disturbance. Reference ranges: method-specific.
refs: Sources: IDSA Aspergillosis Guidelines; manufacturer IFU.

name: ZINC
interpretation: Serum Zinc measures the concentration of zinc in serum. Zinc is an essential trace element involved in over 300 enzymatic reactions, immune function, protein synthesis, wound healing, and DNA synthesis. Zinc deficiency causes growth retardation, hypogonadism, impaired immune function (increased susceptibility to infections), dermatitis (acrodermatitis enteropathica), diarrhoea, and alopecia. Causes of low zinc: inadequate dietary intake (vegetarian diet, processed foods), malabsorption (Crohn disease, coeliac disease), chronic alcoholism, chronic kidney disease, diabetes mellitus, medications (ACE inhibitors, thiazides), burns, and critical illness. Elevated serum zinc is rare and may occur with zinc supplementation toxicity (nausea, vomiting, copper deficiency). Serum zinc is affected by diurnal variation (higher in morning), fasting status (lower in fasting), and inflammation (acute phase response lowers zinc). Limitations: serum zinc does not reflect total body zinc stores. Zinc is largely intracellular and plasma zinc represents only about 0.1 percent of total body zinc. Reference ranges: method-specific. Age: neonates and children have higher levels. Diurnal: higher in morning.
pre_analytical: Sample: Serum. Standard venipuncture. Fasting preferred. Preparation: note symptoms (growth retardation, hypogonadism, recurrent infections, dermatitis), medications (ACE inhibitors, thiazides), diet (vegetarian, alcohol), chronic disease. Handle: avoid zinc contamination from collection tubes. Fasting: preferred (lower in fasting). Diurnal: higher in morning. Inflammation: lowers zinc. Reference ranges: method-specific.
ref_ranges: Normal: 60 to 120 ug/dL (method-specific). Low: less than 60 ug/dL (deficiency). High: greater than 120 ug/dL (toxicity, supplementation). Acrodermatitis enteropathica: markedly low. Diurnal: higher in morning. Fasting: lower. Inflammation: lowers. Reference ranges: method-specific.
refs: Sources: WHO Zinc Deficiency Guidelines; manufacturer IFU.

name: ZNT8 (ZINC TRANSPORTER 8) ANTIBODY
interpretation: Serum Zinc Transporter 8 (ZnT8) Antibody detects autoantibodies against the zinc transporter 8 protein expressed in pancreatic beta cells. ZnT8 antibodies: highly specific for type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM). ZnT8: present in 60-80% of new-onset T1DM. Combined with GAD65, IA-2, IAA: increases T1DM prediction sensitivity to greater than 95%. ZnT8: associated with HLA-DR3/DR4. Reference ranges: method-specific.
pre_analytical: Sample: Serum. Standard venipuncture. No fasting required. Preparation: note diabetes, family history of T1DM, autoimmune disease. Handle per standard. ZnT8: T1DM specific. Combined: GAD65, IA-2, IAA. Reference ranges: method-specific.
ref_ranges: Normal: negative. Positive: T1DM risk. Combined: greater than 95% sensitivity. ZnT8: HLA-linked. Reference ranges: method-specific.
refs: Sources: ADA Diabetes Guidelines; manufacturer IFU.
